title: Literals are Lvalues
prompt: Implement `size_t literal_addr_delta(void)`: take the address of the string literal `"ca"` twice (two separate `&"ca"[0]` expressions), return the byte distance between them as a size_t (0 if equal). Then implement `int literal_is_lvalue(void)` returning 1 unconditionally — because taking that address compiled at all, proving literals are lvalues (modifying them would be UB, not a compile error).

tests.name: addresses comparable
tests.hint: Both expressions designate the same pooled literal on this compiler — distance 0.

tests.name: lvalue proof
tests.hint: Address-of on a literal only compiles for lvalues.
